standard_prerequisites.name: An open immersion is a morphism locally of finite type, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Lets an open subscheme of a J-2 scheme be treated as a scheme locally of finite type over it, which is what the transfer assertion of the lemma needs.

standard_prerequisites.name: A composition of morphisms locally of finite type is locally of finite type, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows a scheme locally of finite type over an open of the base to be viewed as locally of finite type over the base itself.

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a J-2 ring, in the form that every finite type algebra over it has open regular locus, cited from the more algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the ring-level content of the J-2 condition, which is used in both directions of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: A morphism locally of finite type is characterized by finite type ring maps on affine opens, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns local finiteness of type of the morphism into finiteness of type of the induced ring maps, so that the regular locus statement becomes available on affine pieces.

core_obligations: Prove the transfer assertion and the implications that follow from it: an open immersion and a composite of morphisms locally of finite type are again locally of finite type, so a J-2 scheme has J-2 open subschemes and every scheme locally of finite type over it is J-2, which yields (1) implies (3) and (2) implies (4), while (1) implies (2) and (3) implies (4) are immediate because each of the conditions is local on an open covering (proof lines 3326-3341).

Close the cycle by proving (4) implies (1): given the affine open covering S = union of the U_i with each O(U_i) J-2, take a morphism Y to X locally of finite type, cover Y by affine opens V_j each mapping into some U_i, use the characterization of locally finite type morphisms to see that O(U_i) to O(V_j) is of finite type, deduce that each regular locus Reg(V_j) is open, and conclude that Reg(Y) is open because Reg(Y) meets V_j in Reg(V_j) (proof lines 3344-3353).
proof_roadmap: Derive the transfer assertion and the implications that follow from it out of stability of locally finite type morphisms under open immersion and composition, then prove (4) implies (1) by covering a scheme locally of finite type over X by affine pieces on which the regular locus is open (proof lines 3326-3353).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states four equivalent formulations of the J-2 property for a locally Noetherian scheme and adds that every scheme locally of finite type over such a scheme is J-2 (statement lines 3309-3323). The counted proof is a 30-line argument with real content: the transfer statement is derived from stability of locally finite type morphisms under open immersion and composition, the implications (1) to (3) and (2) to (4) are then formal because the conditions are local on an open covering, and the only substantial direction, (4) implies (1), is proved by covering a scheme locally of finite type over X by affine opens V_j mapping into the affines U_i of the assumed covering, converting local finiteness of type into finiteness of type of the ring maps O(U_i) to O(V_j), and concluding openness of the regular locus from the equality of Reg(Y) intersect V_j with Reg(V_j) (proof lines 3326-3353). It is H2 under the lane rule for short proofs: the proof contains a checkable reduction and a genuine local-to-global step rather than a restatement, and the one definitional citation it makes (at proof line 3337) cites the definition of a J-2 ring, not an omitted argument.
